column1: # Proposed identifiers for elevated functions. Source of truth; consumed by
# tools/name_evidence.py, which fills the `Proposed` column of docs/names.md
# and generates docs/name-proposals.md grouped by subsystem.
# Renaming is still deferred (see docs/names.md). This file is the accumulating
# decision, not the rename itself. A bulk rename is byte-neutral -- names do not
# survive objcopy -- so `make compare` proves any eventual application of it.
#   proposed   the identifier to rename it to
#   basis      read | named | read+callee | read+family  (see docs/names.md)
#              read+callee  purpose pinned by reading an already-elevated callee
#              read+family  purpose pinned by a sibling that shares the body
#   subsystem  what part of the ROM it belongs to
#   home       where it would live under a semantic layout
#   why        one line: what in the body justifies the name
# A function whose identity the code does not establish gets an Unk<offset> or
# Unk<n> suffix and says so in `why`. Do not guess a game-facing name.

column6: why
Keeps the ROM's own name; body agrees -- scans the 15 slots at unit+0xd8 for the first equipped entry (0x200) whose info record carries the requested kind, returns the slot index or -1.
The same scan as GetEquippedItem but returns the ItemInfo record rather than the slot index, and takes the unit directly instead of looking it up.
Third member of the trio; same scan, returns the item id masked to 0x1ff. Still parked, named here so the three are renamed together.
53 calls: GiveDjinni then SetDjinni for elements 0-3 across four party slots, then CalcStats on all four. A test fixture, not reachable play.
Builds a 13x5 window at g+0x10, attaches a text layer, stores the handle at g+0x14, writes both OBJ priorities and the 0xff/0 no-selection sentinel. Returns the window.
Walks 64 actor records at iwram_3001e64 (stride 0x70), skipping empty, non-collidable (+0x59 & 1) and self, asking Func_800eba0 for radius overlap. Returns -1 on the first hit.
Twin of Actor_IsBlockedAt, identical but for returning the overlapping record or NULL.
With five or fewer turns left, rolls (luck*3 - turnsLeft*5 + strength) * 0x28f against RPGRandom() & 0xffff. The reason every TickStatusCounter rolls at all.
Counter at unit+0x132, companion signed byte 0x133, recovery strength 0x1e. Which status effect this is is not established by the body.
Counter 0x134, companion 0x135, strength 0x14. Effect identity not established by the body.
Counter 0x136, companion 0x137, strength 0x14. Effect identity not established by the body.
Counter 0x138, no companion, strength 0x1e. Effect identity not established by the body.
Counter 0x139 -- odd, so pooled rather than built with mov+lsl. Strength 0x3c.
Counter 0x13a, strength 0x46 -- the highest in the family, so the easiest effect to shake off early.
Counter 0x13b (odd, pooled), strength 0x28.
Counter 0x13c, strength 0x32.
Counter 0x13d, and the one real variant: a 3-bit count with a carry above it, brought under 8 first, decremented only when the low bits are set, failed outright above 7.
Counter 0x13e, and the only member with no recovery roll and no companion -- hence the bare push {lr} prologue.
Twelfth family member, in its own TU: counter 0x13f (odd, pooled), no companion, no recovery roll.

Draws one decimal digit glyph into a tilemap buffer: 32-byte source rows at .Lb3d40 + digit*32, destination slot from .Lb413c[slot], four 2x2 writes at +0/+1/+30/+31 advancing by four, a zero byte ending the glyph early. Its caller Func_80b0744 passes value % 10, which is what establishes `digit` -- an earlier proposal of UI_DrawIconRow was made without that caller in view and was wrong.
Picks the item container: argument zero gives the party's shared block at ewram_200024c, anything else gives unit 0x83's. Func_807a550 walks the result at +8.
Copies n bytes between two buffers in whichever direction the fourth argument selects -- the save/load direction switch, one routine serving both.
Sets flag 0x20 then runs Func_8079ae8 and CalcStats over units 0, 1 and 5 -- the three starting members recomputed together.
Empty body. Named as a null sub so the ROM slot is accounted for rather than silently dropped.
Clamps the argument to 0..maxHP (unit+0x34), stores it as current HP (unit+0x38), then recomputes the 0..0x4000 bar fraction at unit+0x14.
The PP twin of SetUnitHP: clamps to 0..maxPP (unit+0x36), stores current PP (unit+0x3a), and refreshes the same bar fraction from HP.
Returns 1 for anything Func_8078480 says is not class-restricted, otherwise defers to CanEquipItem. The permissive wrapper around the class-mask test.
Returns 1 if the lead unit or any listed member has a free slot -- FindEmptyInventorySlot returning anything other than 0xf.
Reads the item in the slot, delegates the removal to Func_80788c4, and on success notifies Func_8078ad0 and the UI hook _Func_8091858.
A pure tail call to Func_80792c4. The name follows that callee and should be revisited when it is named; nothing in this body claims more.
Fills the caller's buffer with one id per living party member, taken from gState+0x1f8, and returns the count. Null buffer returns zero.
Adds a delta to the signed byte at gState+0x11c and clamps it to 0..0x1c. Which counter this is is not established by the body.
Indexes .L88db8 as a four-wide table: row times four plus column. A plain accessor; the table's meaning is not established here.
Fills four output stats, each ten times a packed byte. Ids above 7 read the enemy row via GetEnemyInfo and .L88e38 at stride 24; ids 0-7 read the unit's own block at +0x24.
One stat of the four GetBaseStatSpread produces, divided back down by ten. Out-of-range indices return zero.
Looks up the unit's enemy row in .L88e38 (24-byte stride, clamped at 0x2b) and returns its first word.
Builds the full stat spread for a unit, taking the enemy table branch when unit+0x129 is zero and the class branch otherwise.
Recomputes the unit's class byte at +0x129 from its id and Djinn block, then refreshes the derived stats. Paired with CalcStats at every call site.
Allocates a buffer, DMAs the ARM routine Func_8001dc8 into it, calls it on the caller's argument, and frees it. The generic run-from-RAM trampoline.
Scans the sixteen slot-status bytes at iwram_3001f1c for zeros, and returns a random free index, the single free one, or 0x10 for none.
Reads one 0x1000-byte flash sector into the scratch block, copies its sixteen-byte header out, and returns the recomputed checksum minus the stored one -- zero meaning intact.
Resolves the current slot, verifies its sector, then DMA-copies 0xff0 bytes of save payload to the caller. Returns 1 when the slot index is out of range.

Clears a sixteen-byte entry, seeds it from the eight-byte template at .L79b8, and hands it to Func_8005868 for the given channel. SUBSYSTEM UNCERTAIN -- it sits in the flash-save file but the record it fills was read as a sound-channel struct at elevation time. Re-check before renaming.
Walks the block hanging off ewram_2002240+0x28 accumulating a sum and writing it back into the state record. SUBSYSTEM UNCERTAIN in the same way as Func_8005b64.
Reserves the module's 0xa70-byte IWRAM block, primes the field layer, allocates and uploads the sprite sheet, and starts Func_80b00f4 as the module's task.
Allocates a 0x400-byte EWRAM tile buffer, seeds it from .Lb3e80, draws the value one digit at a time with UI_DrawDigit dividing by ten, uploads it as sprite graphics and frees the buffer.
Two DMA transfers from the module's fifth buffer into the field layer's tile area at +0x236, then the two panel hooks _Func_8091200 and _Func_8091254.
Reads the active record off iwram_3001f2c and, when it is non-null, opens message 0xc8a against it and lays out the window with the party's coin total.
The item's base price, zeroed when info[3] bit 3 marks it unsellable, halved for one item class and otherwise three quarters -- the shop's buy-back formula.
Flag-gated once per shop id: sets the visited flag, walks that shop's 0x42-byte row in .Lb41ac and hands each listed entry to _Func_8078ad0.

Answers one of several per-unit condition questions selected by the second argument -- downed at +0x38, the signed byte at +0x131, the byte at +0x140 and so on. Which condition each index means is not established by this body.
Offsets a base message id by the gap between _MSG_d24 and one of _MSG_d2e/_MSG_d38/_MSG_d42, chosen by the state byte at iwram_3001f2c+0x3aa.
Fills a 512-word buffer in four runs -- 32 words of 0x01ff01ff, 240 stepping by 0x00020002 from 0x00010000, 48 more of 0x01ff01ff and 192 zeroes. A packed pair of 16-bit ramps.
Initialises the 0x400-entry dictionary at ewram_2004c00, writing each entry's index alongside a zeroed link field.
Block-copies a w by h rectangle inside the 128-word-wide gBuffer from (sx,sy) to (dx,dy), a row at a time.
Sets BG1CNT to 0x682 and DMAs 0x9600 bytes of gBuffer to the BG1 map at 0x6006a00.
The tile-data twin: BG1CNT 0x501, 0x8000 bytes from ewram_2038000 to 0x6008000.
Brings up the map view: installs the per-frame hook Func_801179c, uploads the background and waits out the fade.
Loads and LZ-decompresses file _FILE_d5 into gBuffer, then installs the view's hooks.
Writes 0 to the halfword at +0x22 of marker record i (12-byte stride) in the table at iwram_3001e70.
The mirror of Map_ClearMarker, writing 1 into the same halfword.
Registers Func_801179c as a per-frame hook, but only while the state byte at +0xfc is zero.
The unregister half of Map_AddRedrawHook, gated on the same byte.
Registers Func_80119cc as a per-frame hook, unconditionally.
Unregisters Func_80119cc.
Reserves the 0xb4-byte EWRAM block under tag 0x1c and zeroes its four marker rows.
Starts Func_8011bf4 at priority 200 << 4.
Stops Func_8011bf4 and releases the tag-0x1c block.
Sign-extends the byte at the pointer and shifts it left 19 -- a tile height into the engine's fixed-point scale.
The same conversion taking the address as an integer rather than a pointer. One of three spellings of one operation in this bank.
The third spelling, loading through a named local first. Kept distinct because the ROM has three separate routines.
Reads the tile byte for a layer at a world position, indexing gBuffer through the layer's 0x30-byte block at +0x130.
Returns the top two bits of byte 1 of the 4-byte gBuffer cell covering (x/16, y/16) -- the cell's collision class.
Resolves a 3D position to a terrain code: a 64x64 cell index into the map at 0x6005000, then a sub-cell nibble out of ewram_202c800.
Returns 0 for terrain codes 5 through 12 and -1 otherwise -- the walkability test over GetTerrainAt.
Combines the terrain code with the height byte from ewram_2020000 for the 32x32 coarse cell, writing the adjusted ground height out.
Writes the three camera words at +4/+8/+0xc of the view record, skipping any argument that is negative.
Walks a layer group's ten sprite entries and points each at the requested animation in the group's sprite info.
Binds a layer group's ten sprite entries to a sprite resource via InitSpriteLayer.
Sums the tile counts of a sprite's parts from its info block, bounded by the part count at info[5].
Permutes one step of a sprite's VRAM tiles through the .L1314c order table -- the dissolve effect's per-step worker.
Drives ScrambleSpriteTiles four steps a frame across all 0x80 steps, waiting a frame between groups.
Empty body.
Empty body, immediately after NullSub_800c0c4.
Installs the script at .L13590 on an actor. What that script does is not established here; the name should follow it, as Camera_SetTarget did for 0x135f0.
Installs the script at .L135a8. Same caveat as Actor_InstallScript13590.
Installs the script at .L135c0. Same caveat.
Installs the script at .L135d8. Same caveat.
Writes the two-bit selector inside the sprite byte at +5 as a bitfield. Which selector it is is not established; this is the batch-71 narrow-constant specimen.
Writes the single-bit field inside the sprite byte at +0x1d. Same caveat as Sprite_SetSelectField.
Registers the two per-frame field hooks Func_800c62c and Func_800c880, opens the panel and unblanks.
Unregisters both field hooks and restores the blend register.
Returns 1 unconditionally. A predicate stub; nothing in the body says what it is standing in for.
Returns 1 unconditionally, the twin of ReturnTrue_800c628.
The specific run-from-RAM call for Func_800a494, the same trampoline shape as RunRAMRoutine.
Script opcode: deletes the actor and returns 0. Joins the ActorCmd_* family already named in this bank.
Reads gKeyPress against the map view's slot record and moves the selection. The exact control mapping is not fully established.
Zeroes the counter and coordinate words at +0x7790..+0x779c of the animation context block. Which counters they are is not established here.
Advances the same +0x7790 counter group by one step per call.
Disables DMA3, then re-arms it to feed gBuffer into the window registers at 0x04000040 -- a per-scanline window effect.
Stops the animation task and its blit task, releases the tag, and runs the RAM-resident cleanup.
Copies WIN0H/WIN0V/WIN1H/WIN1V/WININ straight out of the context block at +0x77bc onward into the hardware.
Writes the two words at context +0x77d0/+0x77d4 into the BG2 reference-point registers at 0x04000028.
Uploads the animation's BG palette from the layer table at iwram_3001e74.
Calls the RAM-resident blit routine against the context block at +0x7818.
Drives a register-animation sequence: arms the destination, then steps it frame by frame. The precise effect is not established here.
Calls Func_80cdb24 with mode 1 and then AnimEnd -- the tail shared by one group of animations.
Empty body.
Re-arms DMA3 from the context block at +0x6980 to feed a per-scanline table.
Sets a battle actor's two speed words to 0x20000 and 0x80000 and starts it travelling, then sets its animation.
Copies an n by m tile block between two buffers, row-major, with the source stride carried separately.
Runs PhysMove between two records and then lowers the destination's y by 0x10.
Calls Func_8000888 through a register-held pointer with an explicit bx, the ARM/Thumb interworking trampoline.
Reads gKeyHeld once the context's counter at +0x24 passes 0x7f -- the skip poll. The discarded read is in the ROM too.
Another re-armed DMA3 out of the animation context block, same shape as Anim_DmaWindowRegs.
Empty body.
Empty body.
Stops Func_80f2f10 and releases the tag-0x20 block.
Runs the effect kernel over the module block, passing the block and the halfway point at +0x1000 as the two working buffers.
The same call with a 0x400-byte split instead of 0x1000.
Writes the mode halfword at the head of the module block, if the block exists.
Clamps to 0..0x1f, the GBA blend-coefficient range.
Clamps to at most 0x7c00, leaving negatives alone.
Signed 16-bit divide built out of sign-extended shifts, with the operands pinned to r0 and r3.
Returns (a << 8) / b -- an 8.8 fixed-point divide.
Returns 0x10000 / x, the 16.16 reciprocal.
Returns the fade-state byte at ewram_2003000, the flag WaitMusicFade spins on.
Writes ewram_2003040, XORing rather than assigning when bit 7 of the argument is set.
Returns the byte at ewram_200303c. What it tracks is not established here.
Spins a frame at a time until the fade-state byte clears, giving up after 300 frames.
